newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden FinMin not worried about forced EMU link.
newsitem.headline: Sweden FinMin not worried about forced EMU link.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink on Thursday shrugged off questions about the possibility of Sweden being forced to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) as it had no opt out clause.
Sweden's ruling Social Democrats announced two days ago that Sweden would not be among the first wave to join EMU in January 1999 but left the door open to join at a later date.
Asbrink told parliament he was not worried that Sweden would be forced to join EMU as it had no opt out clause in the Maastricht Treaty, like Denmark and Britain.
"We have no formal 'opt out' but we have, from the beginning, said that we will decide for ourselves," Asbrink said.
Sweden had maintained it has a right to opt out from EMU because of a unilateral declaration it made on entry into the European Union in 1995 when it adopted the Maastricht treaty.
The issue is a sensitive one because it involves an EU country deciding unilaterally not to do something it has already agreed to do on paper.
But it is considered highly unlikely that the EU would try to force a country to adopt the single currency if its government did not want it.
Asbrink said he believed EMU would start as scheduled on January 1, 1999.
"I will finally make clear that it is my view that the monetary union will start according to the scheduled timetable," Asbrink said.
